messages:
maria (infra): thinking out loud — i'd like to propose a proportional 'slab guard' that allocates GPU slab headroom based on recent tail risk, not flat carveouts. want thoughts on routing fallback behavior once a tenant exceeds guard :thinking_face:

devin (sre): curious — how do you measure 'recent tail risk'? p95/p99 token latency? or some slab eviction alarms?

maria (infra): p99.9 of per-call gpu-sched latency over 10m windows + kv-cache churn rate. if those spike beyond threshold we bump a tenant's slab guard proportionally (e.g. 10% => 30% of a slab) rather than full carveout.

choi (allocator): sounds promising. question: when proportional guard triggers, do we prefer routing to dedicated pool or fallback to a cheaper quantized model? both have different cost/latency tradeoffs.

anna (costops): tagging cost note — routing to dedicated has predictable spend but large fixed cost. falling back to quantized model saves tokens/GPU ops but may increase p99 quality regressions and downstream user support. need a cost budget knob.

patrick (product): from app POV prefer graceful degradation with a quality signal. can we attach an eval set and only route to quantized variant when eval drift < X?

maria (infra): yes, plan is multi-criteria: 1) if tenant is premium/dedicated-eligible => prefer dedicated fallback, 2) else consider quantized fallback when quality delta small and latency budget tight, 3) lastly route to region with spare capacity if egress cost delta acceptable.

ops-bot: [alert] eu-west rack-17 slab-evict spike 1718254335 — noisy neighbor signature detected :warning:

devin (sre): saw that alert. i pushed a soft-quarantine for the offending allocation and started a warm-up of nearby warm-pool to soak spill. results so far: p99 down 15ms.

choi (allocator): for the proportional guard math i'm thinking a sliding EWMA of tail * headroom factor. if > threshold then allocate guard = min(max_guard, floor(slab_size * scale)). also add a springback hysteresis window so we don't flip-flop.

maria (infra): exactly. call it 'springback' — after trigger we decay guard over 30m when metrics stable. prevents churning dedications.

anna (costops): can we expose a per-tenant budget label so finance can auto-approve temporary dedicated routing up to X dollars/day? saves manual escalations.

patrick (product): +1. also want observability: show tenant-level guard state (active, cooling, decaying) in console with last-trigger reason.

devin (sre): one more ops note — fallback routing will increase cross-az egress in some cases. recommend a routing policy that prefers intra-az dedicated first, then quantized local, then cross-az spare. that keeps egress costs bounded.

maria (infra): makes sense. next steps: choi to prototype guard alg, devin to sketch quarantine/playbook, anna to propose budget labels, patrick to mock console flag. let's sync tomorrow 11am.

choi (allocator): prototype ETA: EOD Tuesday. i'll include perf sim with synthetic noisy tenants.

anna (costops): i'll draft budget policy and emergency override flow.

patrick (product): i'll add UX wires and add to roadmap.

maria (infra): thanks — i'll post a short RFC once prototype numbers land. :rocket:
